review_type: Static reverse engineering; no specimen code executed

evidence: Livbaad retains every fifth character, starting at one-based position 11 and ending 12 characters before the input end. Founce is derived as Asc(")") - 40 = 1.
The three Execute statements evaluate reconstructed VBScript environment assignments and WScript.Shell.Run, not PowerShell source directly.
Reconstructed command: cmd.exe /v:on /c echo ^%Autentificeringer^% | !Antidemokrat! - ; Run uses window style 0. The environment values carry the assembled PowerShell and its interpreter path.
The PowerShell numeric key spells Nonserially. Subtraction recovers iex, a Base64 decoder expression, a byte-XOR expression, and a character-array join expression.
Base64 then cyclic XOR of embedded literals recovers synchronous ServerXMLHTTP GET, a Google Drive download URL, and a registry staging loop.

A 200 response is stored as Ildelydendes under HKCU:\Reinvasion\Semisavagery. The stage rereads that value, Base64-decodes it, converts it to ASCII, selects substring(157833,34456), and invokes the reconstructed iex on that substring. Existing registry data can skip the download loop.

Concealed remote-code acquisition, hidden interpreter launch, registry payload storage and evaluation establish hostile intent. No final remote response was fetched. GuLoader is an external queue label, not a family identity proven by this script alone.
samples.trait_judgment: Two suspicious concealment traits; neutral primitives cannot by themselves prove the complete hostile chain established by manual decoding.

samples.identification: Damaged StormAttack service-DLL injector, resource-erased variant
evidence: Entry RVA 0x2674 reaches WinMain at 0x401cb0. Configured mode at 0x404120 is 3, selecting 0x401900 and then self-delete routine 0x401390.

0x401900 creates a GUID-derived HKLM Active Setup Installed Components key, writes StubPath with RegSetValueExA at 0x401a4b, reads its own image with CRT I/O, patches hardcoded offsets, writes a copy, and calls CreateProcessA at 0x401b7e.

Other modes drop resource 101 of type DLL through 0x402460, replace LanmanServer Parameters\ServiceDLL in 0x401260, and inject LoadLibraryA using VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory and CreateRemoteThread in 0x401150. Target selection includes calc.exe, notepad.exe and iexplore.exe.
0x401390 obtains its own module and short path, resolves COMSPEC, builds /c del <self> > nul, and calls CreateProcessA followed by ResumeThread.

The entire 40032-byte .rsrc section is zero. Resource extraction cannot succeed with these bytes; the raw layout also differs from the hardcoded self-copy patch offsets. Static injector, registry-persistence and cleanup code remains. Successful installation or a working DDoS payload is not established.
StormServer.dll and both Storm DDoS server/welcome banners corroborate family identity. No ransomware encryption, ransom note or Remcos implementation was found.
samples.trait_judgment: Existing four hostile code-profile traits are accurate; no PE-specific YAML change.

samples.identification: Damaged StormAttack injector with instruction-padding detours
evidence: Same entry, configured mode 3, Active Setup self-copy, service-DLL hijack, DLL injection and self-delete code as the resource-erased variant.

Compared executable .text bytes directly. Three original CALL sites are replaced with jumps into added RWX .htext; the detours call the original targets and run junk instruction sequences. For example 0x401eb0 jumps to 0x40f000, which calls 0x401150 and then runs long self-exchanges; 0x40115e jumps to 0x40f696, which calls 0x4010c0 and then runs push/pop padding.

An embedded PE begins at file offset 0x5060 and retains Storm DDoS DNS strings and command format. It has only .data, .rsrc and .reloc sections, no executable section, and zero bytes at its entry region. Strings do not establish a functioning DDoS engine.
No concrete WannaCry or Remcos behavior supports the collector filename.
samples.trait_judgment: Existing four hostile code profiles and suspicious instruction-padding observations are accurate; no PE-specific YAML change.
